headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage via MemMachine MCP feeding unstructured document parsing; capability conflict and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python interfaces, while unstructured reads documents/files and can process attacker-controlled content. A shared MCP or file bridge can let document text be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine passes untrusted document text from unstructured into an MCP tool call without provenance tags
IF the two agents share a workspace or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Disable automatic tool execution on parsed document text
Add provenance labels to all unstructured outputs before MemMachine consumes them
Route inter-agent messages through a strict allowlist schema
Require manual approval for any MCP action derived from document content

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and unstructured reads local documents/images/text. If they share a workspace, sensitive content can flow from files into MemMachine outputs. Both have allowlisted egress, so leakage is plausible in default deployments even though no direct exfiltration path is documented.
conditions: IF unstructured processes documents containing sensitive user data in a shared directory
IF MemMachine ingests those outputs into its context or memory store
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Restrict MemMachine ingestion to redacted summaries
Mount document inputs read-only for unstructured
Block sensitive folders from unstructured file discovery

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Unstructured can write files, read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; MemMachine can act through REST/Python/MCP. Even without explicit shared-write evidence, overlapping mutable surfaces create coordination risk if both target the same workspace or downstream service. Uncertainty about orchestration means choosing medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared service
IF MemMachine-triggered actions and unstructured file writes occur concurrently
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Disable package installation during shared runs
Run unstructured in a container with a dedicated volume

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can surface conversational context and long-term preferences, and unstructured can transform documents into downstream text. If MemMachine treats parsed output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect travel decisions or stored memory. No verification step is documented, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF unstructured output is fed into MemMachine memory or planning prompts
IF MemMachine acts on parsed text without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step before memory writes
Require source-document citations in parsed outputs
Compare parsed entities against the original document
Limit MemMachine to read-only consumption of parser output

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic data classes, but MemMachine explicitly handles long-term user facts while unstructured processes documents/images/text. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern remains from retention and handling ambiguity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into MemMachine memory
IF unstructured processes documents subject to stricter retention rules
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Document retention settings for both systems
Purge temporary files after each run
Review privacy policies before production use
